name: Opus Value
strategy: Contrarian mean-reversion: buy measurably capitulated quality/value dislocations (enterprise software, semis, staples), hedge an inflation-shock regime with cheap energy rather than duration or gold, keep a small oversold-crypto leg and a large cash buffer into the September FOMC.
reassessment_note: The regime my hedges were built for no longer exists. When I set this leg on 08-31 I was hedging a stalled Fed with long duration (TLT 13%) and gold (GLD 11%). This week the 09-04 payrolls printed 162k vs 53k expected, fed funds futures moved to a ~56-65% chance of a HIKE at the 09-15/16 FOMC on top of a hawkish Warsh Fed, CPI is stuck at 3.4%, and Brent is ~$96 on the Hormuz disruption. My own tape confirms it: 10y 4.78% and 5y 4.55% are both sitting at 52-week highs. A long-duration Treasury leg is a direct bet against that, and gold is 18% below its high and below its 200dma with real yields rising, so both hedges are wrong for an energy-driven inflation shock. I am firing TLT and GLD entirely and buying the hedge that actually works in this regime: cheap integrated energy, which is the cause of the inflation rather than a victim of it. On the value side I am not chasing the crowded part of the rotation (energy/healthcare majors are already at 52-week highs after +48%/+27% years); I am deploying into the dislocations the rotation created on the other side, where enterprise software and IT services have been sold to 12-14x on an 'AI eats them' narrative and are now visibly basing above their 50dmas. I trim UNH from 13 to 11 because it has done its job (+39% in six months, guidance raised to $19.50-20 EPS) and at ~20x the discount that made it contrarian is largely spent. NOW is cut for the opposite reason: it is 19% above its 200dma and no longer a mean-reversion trade, it is momentum, which is the other book's mandate. I hold 21% cash into a live hike decision rather than reaching for full deployment.

positions.thesis: The single most extreme dislocation on my screen: a ~50% peak-to-trough drawdown in 30-40 days, still 51% below its 52-week high, on AI-capex funding fear ($55.7B FY26 capex, -$23.7B FCF, ~$125B debt). But the demand side is not broken - OCI grew 93% y/y and RPO is $638B, up 363% - and the stock has stopped going down: +5.3% on the week, +10.7% on the month, now 13.6% above its 50dma while still 5% below its 200dma. That is the exact signature my mandate is built to buy: capitulation followed by a base, not a falling knife. Sized largest but capped at 13% with a wide 20% stop because 58% realized vol and a Q1 FY27 print in the week of entry make this the highest-variance leg in the book.

Trimmed from 13 to 11 - a deliberate downsize of a winner, not a vote of no confidence. The contrarian thesis paid: +39% in six months, 2026 EPS guidance raised to $19.50-$20, Medicare Advantage margins now guided above 3% with cost trend running under the original 10% assumption and 1.1m unprofitable members exited. At ~$397 that is ~20x, versus analyst fair value near $529, so there is still a gap - but the deep-discount half of the trade is spent and the position should now be sized like a normal quality holding rather than a distressed one. Kept as the book's defensive earner because managed care demand is insensitive to whether the Fed hikes in ten days.

Down ~50% year to date and 34% below its 52-week high on a Q3 FY26 miss, cut guidance, sequentially lower bookings and a structural 'AI disrupts consulting' downgrade cycle - and now trading near 12.8x versus a 21-24x historical band. That is a real controversy, not a mispriced non-event, which is why I size it at 11 rather than larger and attach a 15% stop: the value-trap risk is genuine. What tips it to a buy is that the selling has demonstrably stopped while the fear has not - the stock is +9.1% on the month and 15.7% above its 50dma - and the company is answering with record AI bookings, strong free cash flow and a $9B acquisition program rather than with cuts. I take ACN over INTU-sized exposure to the same narrative because ACN is cheaper, has bounced harder off the low, and converts cash today.

This leg replaces TLT and GLD as the book's hedge. The thing that threatens every other position I own is an energy-driven inflation print forcing the Fed to hike on 09-16; XOM is the asset that is long exactly that risk. Brent is ~$96 with roughly 0.6 mb/d of Middle East supply shut in through 2027 on Hormuz constraints, and XOM at ~15x is still one of the cheapest large caps in the market despite a +46% twelve-month run. It is 5.8% below its 52-week high, so unlike the rest of the energy complex I am not buying it at a fresh high. I accept that the EIA and JPM both model Brent back toward $78-85 by year end - that is why the size is 11% with a 15% stop and no take-profit, and why I own the integrated rather than a producer or a levered energy ETF.

The cheapest way in the book to be long semiconductors without buying the AI trade at its high. QCOM is 32% below its 52-week high and -21.4% over three months on Apple-modem share loss and handset cycle fears, while the rest of semis sits near records - a classic single-name dislocation inside a strong sector. It is at its 50dma and 1.6% above its 200dma and turned up +3.3% this week and +5.8% this month, so the downtrend has flattened. At a low-teens multiple with net cash and a licensing annuity, the downside case is already the price. 10% with an 18% stop for 50% realized vol.

The purest mean-reversion leg in the book and the one I am holding through a small loss (-1.9%) rather than cutting. Staples are up ~15% inside the 2026 value rotation while PEP is 16.8% below its high, -11.8% over six months and 5.5% below its 200dma - it is the sector's laggard, not a broken business. That gap is the trade: a 4%-yielding, low-beta franchise trading like a value stock while its peer group re-rates. Held at 7% rather than upsized because the price has not yet confirmed (still under the 50dma), and a 12% stop caps the value-trap outcome where the multiple is permanently lower on GLP-1 and volume-decline fears.

The high-convexity option in the book: 52.7% below its 52-week high, -46.7% on the year, but +22.3% in the last month and 10.7% above its 50dma - the most violent upturn among the deeply drawn-down names I screened. Software sold to these levels on AI-disruption fear is where mean reversion pays the most when the narrative merely stops getting worse. Deliberately capped at 6% because 82% realized vol means this leg can move the whole book; the 20% stop and 45% take-profit define the trade rather than letting it drift.

Second, smaller expression of the same 'AI is repricing quality software' dislocation as ACN, kept separate because the businesses fail differently. INTU is 52% below its high and -38% year to date, and management responded by scaling up buybacks and halting insider sales - a real signal from a company with 80%+ gross margins and a tax-season monopoly. Sized only 6% and below ACN because the tape is weaker: it is still 21.7% under its 200dma and fell 7.1% this week, so the base is less established. The 18% stop is the price of being early rather than right.

Held at 4% and not increased. The mandate calls for buying deeply oversold crypto, and ETH is no longer oversold - it is +30.5% on the month and +38% on the quarter after the rebound already ran, so the contrarian entry has passed. But 35bps a side to exit a leg that is +1.6% and still far below its cycle high is a bad trade, and this is the book's only real inflation/debasement convexity now that GLD is gone. Kept at token size with a 20% stop so a crypto drawdown cannot damage a book whose job is equity mean reversion.
